clue.text: Uniformed youngster displays nothing that's in style

parts.note: airs are showy displays or affected manners, as in putting on airs

indicators.note: 'that's in' tells us the word for nothing sits inside the word for style

parts.note: a cut is a style, as of a garment or a haircut
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A young person in uniform shows off with nothing fashionable about them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. An Air Scout belongs to the aviation branch of the Scout movement, whose members wear a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a member of the aviation branch of Scouting, who wears its uniform.

clue.text: Ishmael heartlessly disturbed prophet

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of order, so the remainder is rearranged
without its heart, the central letter of the seven-letter name is removed

explanation.surface: Ishmael, the outcast son of Abraham, is cruelly upset by a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes the central M from ISHMAEL, leaving ISHAEL; 'disturbed' rearranges those six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the Old Testament seer who succeeded Elijah, so a biblical prophet.

clue.text: Rhubarb desserts?

definitions.meaning: rhubarb is British slang for nonsense or rubbish talk
fruit puddings topped with a scone-like crust, a common way to bake rhubarb

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures rhubarb puddings, which fits a fruit dessert, but rhubarb here is the British word for nonsense; the British slang word for nonsense is also the name of those baked puddings.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for rubbish talk; also the name of baked fruit puddings with a biscuit-dough topping.

clue.text: Drinking receptacle allowed to touch mouth

indicators.note: 'to touch' places the word for allowed right against the word for mouth, side by side

parts.note: gob is British slang for the mouth
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: A drinking vessel that may be lifted to the lips.
explanation.walkthrough: GOB is everyday British slang for the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: A stemmed drinking glass or cup is a classic vessel to drink from.

clue.text: Newspaper article about a session in the spa?

indicators.note: 'about' means the newspaper's name goes round the following letter a

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A journalist writes a piece on an outing to a health spa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside SUN to make SAUN, and the article A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam bath is a typical treatment taken during a visit to a spa.

clue.text: Madison Square empty, surprisingly, in heart of winter?

indicators.note: surprisingly signals that the letters land in an unexpected order
an empty word loses all its inner letters, keeping only its first and last

explanation.surface: New York's Madison Square is deserted, oddly, in the depths of winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' reduces Square to SE; 'surprisingly' rearranges MADISON plus SE.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle part of any season, so the heart of winter is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Call councillor amid havoc near south London terminal

indicators.note: 'near' places the south abbreviation right next to the rest, at its end
'amid' puts the call and councillor in the middle of the word for havoc

parts.note: havoc means chaos or disorder
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A councillor gets a phone call during chaos at a big London railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' is the container signal and 'near' just adds the last letter. Charing Cross is a main-line railway station in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: A main-line railway station in central London, the end of the line for trains from the south-east.

clue.text: Hollywood folk, maybe, performing in French director's biblical work

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is home to Hollywood
folk are people, here men

indicators.note: 'in' places the word for performing inside the director's name and possessive

parts.note: Jacques Tati was a French film director; with 's he gives TATIS
on means performing, as an actor on stage

explanation.surface: Some Hollywood actors appear in a French filmmaker's version of a Bible story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'Hollywood folk, maybe' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two pieces; 'maybe' admits that such men are only one sort of Hollywood folk.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of the Old Testament mourning the fall of Jerusalem, traditionally credited to Jeremiah.

clue.text: Time and place during holiday for live entertainment

indicators.note: 'during' puts the time and place inside the word for holiday

parts.note: a stay is a visit or short holiday somewhere
an age is a long period of time
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A theatre outing is booked for a set time and venue while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is the container signal; 'Time' looks like a clock reading but stands for a long era.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama performed by actors on a stage in front of an audience, as opposed to film or radio.

clue.text: He wrote volume in French about revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so these two short words are read backwards together

parts.note: en is the French word for in
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An author produced a book in French about a radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a noun for a radical, but it turns the two short words round together. Jules Verne was the French author of science-fiction adventures.
explanation.definitionFit: A French novelist, so a person who wrote; the clue names him only as an author.

clue.text: The mass starts with a new hymn

indicators.note: 'starts with' says the following pieces come first, at the front

parts.note: taken as written
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A church mass begins with an unfamiliar song of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts with' puts A and N in front of THE and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A song of praise or loyalty, such as a church choral piece or a national song.

clue.text: Female has row in supermarket stocking Irish knitwear

indicators.note: 'stocking' means holding the Irish abbreviation inside, as a shop stocks goods

parts.note: an aisle is a row of shelves in a supermarket

explanation.surface: A woman finds a supermarket aisle selling Irish woollens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' is the container signal, not hosiery. Fair Isle knitting is named after a Shetland island, so it is in fact Scottish, not Irish.
explanation.definitionFit: A style of multicoloured patterned jumper from a Shetland island, so a kind of knitwear.

clue.text: Aim of lonely hearts' club member until now

definitions.text: Aim of lonely hearts' club member
definitions.meaning: someone joining a singles club wants to go out romantically with a partner

explanation.surface: A singles club joiner's purpose so far.
explanation.walkthrough: A lonely hearts' club is a dating club; its members wish to find someone to take out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the wish of a singles-club joiner (going out with someone) and an idiom meaning so far.

clue.text: Worshipped by fans, I perform song about start of show

parts.note: to do is to perform

indicators.note: 'about' means the song goes round the letter taken from show

parts.note: a lied is a German art song

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A singer boasts of being adored after opening a show with a number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' gives S from show and 'about' is the container signal. A lied (plural lieder) is a German art song.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored or revered as a star, which is how fans treat their heroes.

clue.text: Expert copper's put in charge

indicators.note: 'put in' places the copper symbol and its S inside the word for expert

parts.note: an ace is an expert
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: A skilled police officer has been placed in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal, chemical symbol Cu; 'put in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone is to formally allege that they did wrong, a verb of blame.

clue.text: Put an end to rugby match

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
a bout is a match or contest, as in boxing

explanation.surface: Calling off a rugby game.
explanation.walkthrough: RU is Rugby Union, the fifteen-a-side game.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang verb for killing or eliminating, so to finish someone off.

clue.text: Name most of African country after a former British PM

indicators.note: 'after' sets the shortened country behind the letter a

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Ghana is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A former British premier is named after most of an African state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the country's last letter. James Callaghan was UK Labour Prime Minister from 1976 to 1979.
explanation.definitionFit: James Callaghan was Labour Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1976 to 1979.

clue.text: Pre-Euro currency sailor deposited in a French bank, not surprisingly

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: 'deposited in' puts the currency and sailor inside the word for bank, like money paid in

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
the mark was Germany's currency before the euro
AB, able seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor pays old German money into a bank in France, as anyone would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a building but is a verb, as in to bank on someone. 'deposited in' is the container signal. The mark was West Germany's currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Means in an ordinary, unexceptional way, so as might be predicted.

clue.text: Inaccurate book losing jacket in London school

indicators.note: 'in' places the middle of book inside the school's initials

parts.note: the LSE is the London School of Economics

indicators.note: a book losing its jacket is stripped of its outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A careless textbook lost its dust jacket at a London college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing jacket' strips book to its middle letters and 'in' is the container signal. The LSE is the London School of Economics.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking precision, as a free or rough translation is not exact.

clue.text: Very confused over musical work, piece for organ

indicators.note: in a down clue 'over' means the preceding words sit above the musical work

parts.note: so means very
lost means confused or bewildered
op, opus, is a numbered musical work

explanation.surface: A muddled musician puzzles over a composition for the church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sets SO LOST above OP in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An organ register (a part of the instrument) that makes a voice suited to playing a melody alone.

clue.text: … Stainer's composed, showing such cultural pretension

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Sir John Stainer was a Victorian church composer; his name with its S gives the fodder

explanation.surface: Following on, a Victorian church composer's music displays airy cultural affectation.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the organ clue before it. 'composed' rearranges the eight letters of STAINER'S, the possessive S included. John Stainer wrote church music.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretentious show of being cultured or sophisticated in art, which 'such' ties to the ellipsis.

clue.text: Personal document I had with certainty transcribed on back of pad

indicators.note: 'on' in a down clue puts the preceding pieces on top of the last piece

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: transcribed means written out anew, so the letters are set in a new order
the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone writes that they were sure of themselves on the back of a notepad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transcribed' rearranges CERTAINTY into ENTITYCAR; 'back of' gives D from pad; 'on' puts ID and ENTITYCAR above that D.
explanation.definitionFit: An official card carried by a person to prove who they are.

clue.text: Name of cape in US state with water on either side

indicators.note: 'on either side' means the waterway is split to stand at each end of the word for state

parts.note: a canal is a man-made waterway
to aver is to state or declare

explanation.surface: A headland in America is in a state with sea on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US state' reads as one idea, but US belongs to the definition and 'state' is a verb. 'on either side' wraps the waterway round. Cape Canaveral is the Florida launch site.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Canaveral, in Florida, is the headland known for American space launches.

clue.text: Impressive person's kind deed

parts.note: a class is a kind or category
an act is a deed

explanation.surface: Someone splendid performs a good deed.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for an outstanding, stylish person or performer.

clue.text: Revealed my spouse has left me?

definitions.meaning: disclosed or passed on, as news or knowledge
split two ways the letters say the speaker is now separated from a partner

explanation.walkthrough: The second part is a whimsical reading: as two words the answer is what a deserted husband or wife might say, 'I am separated', hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Told or made known, as information is passed on; and, split after the first two letters, a lament of being separated.

clue.text: Emergency as camper losing contents over river

indicators.note: in a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the river
a word that loses its contents keeps only its outside letters

parts.note: the Isis is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford

explanation.surface: A camper's gear is emptied out over a river, causing a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing contents' takes camper down to CR; 'over' puts it above ISIS, the stretch of the River Thames at Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: A time of intense danger or difficulty demanding urgent action.

clue.text: 27 player in side getting goal?

indicators.note: 'getting' joins the side to the goal, which follows it

parts.note: leg is the on side of a cricket field
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A star footballer on the team scores a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is IDOLISED, so the definition is an idolised player. Leg, in cricket, is the half of the field on the batter's side.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports star who is hero-worshipped, a famous and revered performer.

clue.text: Standing up in important ceremony

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the letters run from bottom to top, so they read backwards
'in' says the letters are tucked inside the words important ceremony

explanation.surface: Upright posture is required at a solemn occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds TCERE across importanT CEREmony, and 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright, on one's feet rather than sitting or lying.
